workflow_hypothesis: Reachability-unaware code generation produces compiler diagnostics
pattern: Generated control flow retains unreachable operations after termination or configuration folding
description: Code generation preserves mechanically emitted statements or control-flow constructs after a handler has already terminated, or when configuration folding makes a branch or loop impossible.
precondition: Generated handlers combine explicit returns or jumps with generic cleanup/error emission, and some conditions or operation paths are compile-time fixed by configuration.
critical_operation: The generator emits the handler body and then appends cleanup, error-handling, or loop code using a fallthrough-oriented reachability model.
interference: An internal return/jump, or a compile-time constant condition, makes the appended statement or branch unreachable, while the generator still places it in the generated source.
invalid_assumption: The generator assumes every emitted continuation remains reachable and that conditionally emitted paths should be treated as runtime possibilities, rather than tracking termination and configuration-specific dead paths.
failure: The compiler reports unreachable-code or unused-code diagnostics in generated low-level source; warning-as-error configurations can fail the build.
search_strategy: Inspect generated handlers for statements emitted immediately after return or unconditional jump tokens.
Trace generator reachability state through return, jump, and error-label emission, and verify later cleanup is suppressed when the path terminates.
Search generated output under each supported compile-time configuration for constant-false branches and loops with provably non-executing bodies.
Compare generic stack or resource cleanup emission against handlers that return from inside an operation rather than at the normal epilogue.

evidence.supports: The report documents unreachable cleanup after generated returns or jumps, loops whose conditions become statically impossible, and configuration-defined false error branches; subsequent fixes remove dead generated paths and teach the generator to mark return-following tokens unreachable.

scope_note: This is a cautiously scoped pattern from a singleton report. It covers generators that combine generic control-flow/cleanup templates with compile-time configuration folding; it does not claim that all compiler unreachable-code warnings originate in code generation.
